title: Abstract Tate residue and its basic invariances
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $C$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $V$ a $C$-module. For $f\in C$ write $m_f(v)=fv$. Call a $k$-subspace $A\subseteq V$ admissible if $(m_f A+A)/A$ is finite-dimensional over $k$ for every $f\in C$. An endomorphism $T$ of a $k$-vector space is finite-potent if $T^N(V)$ is finite-dimensional for some $N\geq1$; its Tate trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(T)$ is the ordinary trace on a finite-dimensional $T$-stable subspace containing $T^N(V)$, independent of these choices. For every admissible $A$ there is a unique $k$-linear map $\operatorname{res}_{V,A}:\Omega^1_{C/k}\to k$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] such that for every $k$-linear projection $\pi:V\to A$ and every $f,g\in C$, the endomorphism $[\pi m_f,m_g]=\pi m_fm_g-m_g\pi m_f$ is finite-potent and
$$\operatorname{res}_{V,A}(f\,dg)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}([\pi m_f,m_g]).$$
This residue is independent of $\pi$. It is unchanged under $C$-linear isomorphisms of pairs $(V,A)$. If $W\subseteq V$ is a $C$-submodule containing $A$, then $\operatorname{res}_{W,A}=\operatorname{res}_{V,A}$. If either $A$ or $V/A$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, then $\operatorname{res}_{V,A}=0$. If $m_f A\subseteq A$ and $m_g A\subseteq A$, then $\operatorname{res}_{V,A}(f\,dg)=0$; in particular $\operatorname{res}_{V,A}=0$ when $A$ is a $C$-submodule.
